topics.label: Introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This section introduces the lecture topic, connects it to practical class observations, and outlines the key learning outcomes.

topics.label: Tumor virology, oncogene discovery, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how the study of transforming viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and established laboratory assays for measuring cell transformation.

topics.label: Oncogenes, tumor suppressors, and cell cycle checkpoints
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the functional classification and genetic mechanisms of oncogenic and tumor-suppressive mutations using key regulators such as Rb and p53.

topics.label: Mechanisms and consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how defects in DNA repair, replication fidelity, and chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosome instability in cancer cells.

topics.label: Multi-step tumorigenesis and hereditary cancer predispositions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how the stepwise accumulation of somatic mutations and inherited genetic predispositions drive tumor progression and adaptation.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and reading recommendations
topics.groupedBecause: This section concludes the lecture, offers recommended background reading, and previews the next session.
